goal: Make Control Plane node health truthful: stale heartbeats must not be presented as fully online, and the owner must see fresh/degraded/stale node counts clearly.
objective: On a server node, inspect and repair or document the Control Plane node freshness contract. The current /v1/nodes response reported 42 node cards, 32 health=online, but only 9 nodes with heartbeat <=30 minutes and 33 stale >30 minutes. Create tests and a focused PR or exact blocker report so stale nodes are classified truthfully and the factory wallboard/API cannot overstate online capacity.
required_analysis: Find where /v1/nodes and /v1/fleet style node status is computed.
Define freshness thresholds for fresh, stale, degraded, offline and unknown states.
Check whether stale heartbeat cards should be excluded from online counts or returned with health=stale/degraded.
Check factory panel /api/factory/status mapping so owner-facing online node counts are not inflated.
Do not delete node records; preserve identity/history while marking freshness truthfully.
implementation_options: If the contract is missing but safe to repair, add focused tests and a PR branch that classifies stale heartbeats truthfully.
If live behavior differs from repo code, produce exact blocker and deployment/runbook task instead of guessing.
If existing code already has freshness logic, identify why production endpoint still reports stale nodes as online and create the smallest repair task.
acceptance: Remote execution happens on a server/control node.
Current stale/online mismatch is reproduced or classified with exact evidence.
A focused PR is opened if code repair is safe, otherwise an exact blocker/runbook task is produced.
Stale heartbeats are not counted as fully online in the proposed contract.
No product code is modified on Mac.
No service restart or live runtime mutation occurs in this task.
Final result gives the next exact deployment/canary task.
